Subject: Acme POC: Integration plan, success criteria & next steps

Thanks again for the call this morning — great to meet you both. Quick recap and proposed next steps for the POC/trial: 

Summary of ask
- Evaluate Redwood for in-product assistant and content generation across three flows (help center summarization, inline suggestions, autosuggest responses).
- Goal: prove parity with current solution on latency and cost while improving quality of summaries.

Success criteria (proposed)
1) Latency: 95th percentile <= 350ms for single-turn generation under our expected traffic profile (50 rps burst).
2) Cost: tokens/unit cost <= current baseline by >=10% after batching and caching.
3) Quality: NPS-style score on 200 eval prompts >= baseline, and no regressions on top 20 critical prompts.
4) Stability: no sustained errors >1% over a 72h run.

Evaluation plan & timeline
- Week 1 (this week): Integration spike and sample ingest; set up streaming & test harness. (Owner: Acme engineering / Redwood SE)
- Week 2: Run full traffic-shaped tests, collect latency/cost metrics, run eval set. (Owner: Acme + Redwood)
- Week 3: Iterate on prompts / quantization profile, report.

Integration notes (high level)
- We propose using Redwood's SDK for quick proof-of-concept. Streaming for real-time assistant flows and standard REST for batch summarization.
- We'll provide an integration checklist and a short tech doc with example API calls.

Attachments: acme-poc-scope.pdf (scope + success criteria), redwood-integration-checklist.xlsx

Next steps
1) Can you confirm the success criteria above and the owners/timeline?
2) Share a technical contact who can work with Michael and our engineering team on the integration spike.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Thanks — quick technical plan for the spike and owners: 

Spike goals (48-72h)
- Validate p50 < 120ms for suggestion flows using streaming API and continuous batching.
- Exercise tool calling for internal search connector (sample lambda + signed requests).
- Produce sample metrics (p50/p95/p99, error rates, cost per 1k tokens).

Proposed technical approach
1) SDK + streaming: Use Redwood JS SDK (node) with streaming response handler for suggestion flows. Example route: POST /v1/generate/stream with headers Authorization: Bearer <key>. We'll provide an example that uses chunked transfer and our client-side handler to render tokens incrementally.
2) Batch summarization: REST endpoint POST /v1/generate with prompt template and max_tokens. We recommend using our batching hints (X-Redwood-Batch-Hint) to optimize throughput during load testing.
3) KV cache + prefix caching: We'll suggest a short-lived KV cache for repeated context in conversation to reduce repeat compute. Config via SDK: cache: { mode: "prefix", ttl: 300 } (we'll provide sample config file).
4) Tool calling: Use function/schema calls via the model -> tool interface. Example payloads and a minimal auth flow for calling Acme's search API will be in the checklist. We'll run a local mock search endpoint for the spike.

Owners & tasks
- Dev Patel (Staff Engineer, Redwood) — implement streaming example, tool-calling mock, and checklist (owner).
- Michael Grant (Solutions Eng) — integration runbook, load script, metric dashboards (owner).
- Priya Shah (Acme) — provide sample prompt set, top-10 enterprise prompts, and access to a test search endpoint.

Artifacts I'll deliver by Friday EOD:
- node-streaming-example.js (SDK usage)
- generate-rest-sample.json (REST call examples)
- spike-runbook.md (run instructions + perf scripts)

Questions for Marissa/Acme
- Can Priya share a temporary API key for the mock search or a swagger for quick mock?
- Any IP/consent restrictions on sending prompt samples to Redwood infra?

Dev
